documents.title: AI Syllabus Statements
documents.stance_why: The provost document tells instructors to "communicate the extent to which AI use is permitted overall" and gives three degrees of AI use with sample statements for each. It sets no single stance and offers tiers, so stance is delegates.
documents.summary: This Mizzou provost document is a menu of three tiers (prohibited, limited, integration allowed) with sample syllabus language and citation formats for instructors to pick from. It sets no university stance of its own.

units.why: The page tells instructors to "communicate the extent to which AI use is permitted overall", so it is a rule that each course states its AI stance; instructor, course-start, should, type P09 (state AI expectations in the syllabus).
units.resolution_why: Coders differed (phase: A before-course, B course-start). A coded phase before-course, B course-start. Source: 'Start with General Statements About AI Usage to communicate the extent to which AI use is permitted overall' says what the syllabus statement should open with, i.e. communicating expectations to students. course-start matches how the UM System page units on syllabus statements are coded, and the anchor alone states the rule, so policy is null. Final: instructor, course-start, should, P09.
units.anchor: communicate the extent to which AI use is permitted overall
units.fit_note: Frames the statement as a build step for instructors rather than a requirement to include one.

units.why: The sheet tells instructors to 'review examples of transparency guidelines that describe citation and attribution practices' where AI is allowed. It points instructors to sample disclosure wording, so it is sample language for instructors (P110), addressed to instructors, to be read while designing the course (before-course), should.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on actor, phase, modality and type. Both coders coded P24 (disclose AI use with each submission) and both wrote a fit note that the sentence is addressed to instructors, not students. Source: the sentence tells instructors to review example guidelines; it does not itself require disclosure. The nearest type is P110 (provide sample syllabus language and templates), which fits what the sentence does, so the type is changed to P110.
units.anchor: review examples of transparency guidelines that describe citation and attribution practices
units.frag_start: If AI is allowed to any degree,
units.policy: Where AI is allowed to any degree, instructors review examples of transparency guidelines that describe citation and attribution practices.
units.fit_note: (Coders' notes were written for P24.) A: Addressed to instructors who should adopt disclosure guidelines; P24 itself binds students. B: Addressed to instructors: they should provide transparency guidelines; it does not itself require students to disclose.

units.why: The sheet says to 'search for statement examples from faculty in your (or a near) discipline in a spreadsheet with entries from various universities'. This points instructors to a further resource of sample statements, so it is P115 (point to further guidance and resources), instructor, before-course, may.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A kept this as a real unit (coded P63, support faculty in learning AI); A also wrote a duplicate with the same anchor addressed to students (A57, P25), which is dropped. Source: the sentence is addressed to instructors and points to a spreadsheet of statements, not to workshops or consultations, so P115 fits better than P63. Final: instructor, before-course, may, P115.
units.anchor: search for statement examples from faculty in your (or a near) discipline
units.policy: Instructors can search for statement examples from faculty in their or a near discipline in a spreadsheet with entries from various universities.
units.fit_note: (Coders' notes were written for P63.) Peer examples as a resource, not workshops or consultations.

units.why: The sheet sorts sample statements by 'Degree of AI Integration Permitted' into three named degrees, which is a tiered scheme for course AI policy, so P05.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded this overview sentence. Source: the table header 'Degree of AI Integration Permitted' introduces the three degrees (prohibited, limited, integration allowed). Coder B coded each tier description as its own unit, but the overview that names the three-degree scheme is a separate statement, so it is kept as a P05 unit. Final: admin, before-course, informs, P05.
units.anchor: Degree of AI Integration Permitted
units.frag_end: Find helpful icons for all AI positions
units.policy: The provost sheet sorts example syllabus statements into three degrees: AI usage prohibited, limited AI usage permitted, and AI integration allowed.

units.why: The sheet says 'Find helpful icons for all AI positions to use on your syllabi and assignments', pointing instructors to Oregon State's icon set. It points to an outside resource for communicating the course AI position, so P115, instructor, course-start, may.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed (policy_type: A P05, B P09). A coded P05 (tiers), B coded P09 (AI statement in every syllabus). Source: the sentence only points instructors to optional icons from Oregon State; it does not name tiers (P05) and does not require a statement (P09; B's own fit note says so). The nearest fit is P115, point to further resources. Final: instructor, course-start, may, P115.
units.anchor: Find helpful icons for all AI positions to use on your syllabi and assignments

units.policy: Instructors can find icons for all AI positions to use on their syllabi and assignments.

units.why: The table names a tier "AI tools are not allowed for any assignments" under "AI Usage Prohibited"; this is a named level of AI use, so P05, instructors choose it, informs.

units.anchor: AI tools are not allowed for any assignments.
units.policy: One tier instructors may adopt is AI Usage Prohibited: AI tools are not allowed for any assignments.

units.why: The sample says "a strict policy against the use of AI software in any aspect of the learning process"; a course-wide ban is P01 and it binds students.
units.anchor: strict policy against the use of AI software in any aspect of the learning process

units.why: The sample statement says 'Students are expected to rely solely on their own cognitive abilities and academic skills when drafting, editing, and revising assignments'. In a no-AI course this means students may not have AI produce the drafting and editing of submitted work, so P19, with 'expected' read as an expectation that binds (must), during-work.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed (modality: A must, B must-not; policy_type: A P21, B P19). A coded must/P21 (do not use AI to debug or check graded work), B coded must-not/P19. Source: 'rely solely on their own cognitive abilities ... when drafting, editing, and revising' is about not having AI do the writing, not about debugging or checking, so P21 does not fit and P19 does. The sentence is phrased as a positive expectation ('are expected to'), which is must, not must-not. Final: student, during-work, must, P19.
units.anchor: rely solely on their own cognitive abilities and academic skills
units.policy: Students are expected to rely solely on their own cognitive abilities and academic skills when drafting, editing, and revising assignments.
units.fit_note: Also reads as a general ban on AI for writing and editing; chosen P21 because editing and revising are named.

units.why: The statement gives its reason: assessments should 'accurately reflect each student's independent learning and writing capabilities', grounding the ban in honest assessment, so P95 rather than skill-building P41.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed (actor: A all, B admin). Same type and phase; A coded actor all, B admin. Source: 'This course policy is in place to uphold the principle of individual academic achievement' is the rationale of a sample course statement and binds nobody in particular, so actor all. Final: all, general, informs, P95.
units.anchor: assessments accurately reflect each student’s independent learning and writing
units.policy: The course policy is in place to uphold individual academic achievement and to ensure that assessments accurately reflect each student's independent learning and writing capabilities.

Final: all, general, informs, P77.
units.anchor: This policy aligns with the UM System Student Code of Conduct 200.010.

units.anchor: Academic units will create policies related to the use of AI

units.why: The list "organized coursework, 2) supervised research ... 3) qualifying and comprehensive exams, and 4) capstone experiences" sets the scope of the policy, P61.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this. Source: 'in different areas of graduate education: 1) organized coursework, 2) supervised research ..., 3) qualifying and comprehensive exams, and 4) capstone experiences' sets what the policy covers. It is a scope statement distinct from the duty to create policies, so it is kept as P61 with B's fit note. Final: admin, general, informs, P61.
units.anchor: organized coursework, 2) supervised research (or other supervised creative endeavors), 3) qualifying and comprehensive exams
units.policy: The graduate AI policy covers four areas of graduate education: organized coursework, supervised research (or other supervised creative endeavors), qualifying and comprehensive exams, and capstone experiences.
units.fit_note: Defines the scope as four areas of graduate education rather than defining AI.

units.why: 'The goal(s) of the educational experience' must be stated, tying AI rules to objectives, so P83.
units.anchor: The goal(s) of the educational experience
units.policy: Each unit policy states the goals of the educational experience.
units.fit_note: Requires stating goals, not explicitly that AI rules follow from them.

units.why: "Whether AI is permitted" is a required element of every unit policy, so each must state its stance, P09.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this as its own unit. A coded one lump unit for the whole list of elements ('Each policy needs to include the following elements'). Source: 'Whether AI is permitted' is one element in the list; the lump merges distinct rules, so the lump is dropped and the elements are kept separately. P09 is only a partial fit because the rule is about unit policies, not syllabi (fit note). Final: admin, before-course, must, P09.
units.anchor: Whether AI is permitted
units.policy: Each unit policy states whether AI is permitted.
units.fit_note: Applies to unit policies for coursework, research, exams and capstones, not only syllabi.

units.why: "which tasks (and tools, if applicable) are permitted" requires the policy to list allowed tasks and tools, P09.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this as its own unit; A's lump unit covers it (see the previous unit). Source: 'If AI is permitted, specify which tasks (and tools, if applicable) are permitted' is a distinct element of the unit policy. P09 with a fit note, as above. Final: admin, before-course, must, P09.
units.anchor: which tasks (and tools, if applicable) are permitted.
units.policy: If AI is permitted, each unit policy specifies which tasks (and tools, if applicable) are permitted.

units.why: 'how AI use should be disclosed and acknowledged' requires each unit policy to specify disclosure, so P24.
units.anchor: how AI use should be disclosed and acknowledged
units.policy: Where AI is permitted, each unit policy specifies how AI use should be disclosed and acknowledged.
units.fit_note: A: Requires units to specify disclosure rules; does not itself bind students. B: Units must specify disclosure; it does not itself require students to disclose.

units.why: "restrict all uses of AI, permit some uses of AI, or permit all uses of AI" sets three options, P05.
units.anchor: restrict all uses of AI, permit some uses of AI, or permit all uses
units.policy: For each experience, units provide policies that either restrict all uses of AI, permit some uses of AI, or permit all uses of AI.

units.why: 'compliant with ethical, research, and IT guidelines' requires unit policies to follow existing rules, so P77.
units.anchor: All policies created by academic units must be compliant with ethical, research, and IT guidelines
units.policy: All policies created by academic units must be compliant with ethical, research, and IT guidelines from the University of Missouri and other relevant stakeholders, such as granting agencies and publishers.

units.why: 'improper uses of AI is academic dishonesty' classifies misuse as misconduct, so P36.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed (actor: A all, B admin). Same type; actor all (A) vs admin (B). Source: 'Per the Office of Academic Integrity, improper uses of AI is academic dishonesty' is a definition that applies to everyone, so all. Final: all, when-misuse, informs, P36.
units.anchor: improper uses of AI is academic dishonesty
units.policy: Per the Office of Academic Integrity, improper uses of AI are academic dishonesty.

units.why: "faculty will follow the procedures of that office" sends suspected cases to the Office of Academic Integrity process, P81.
units.anchor: in cases of suspected academic dishonesty, faculty will follow the procedures of that office

units.why: The page says 'Individual programs may use or customize templates to suit their policy needs'. The university supplies templates that programs may adopt or adapt, which is P110, addressed to units (admin) as set-up (before-course), may.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed (policy_type: A P05, B P85). A coded P05 (tiers), B coded P85 (units set their own rules). Source: the sentence is about templates that programs may use or customize; it names no tiers (A's own fit note says the page does not describe them), and the right of units to make their own policy is in the first sentence. P110 (sample language and templates) fits what the sentence says. Final: admin, before-course, may, P110.
units.anchor: Individual programs may use or customize templates to suit their policy needs
units.policy: Individual programs may use or customize templates to suit their policy needs.
units.fit_note: (Coders' notes were written for P05/P85.) Templates are offered, but the page does not describe their tiers.

units.why: "Each instructor will have a statement in the syllabus about using AI" requires a graduate syllabus statement, P09.

units.anchor: Appropriate uses, tools, and disclosures of AI may vary by discipline.

units.why: "different capstone experiences ... will have unique goals; thus, different AI guidelines" ties guidelines to goals, P83.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed (phase: A before-course, B general). Same type; phase before-course (A) vs general (B). Source: 'It is possible and perhaps expected that different capstone experiences ... will have unique goals; thus, different AI guidelines' states a principle, not a step of set-up, so general.
